subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.

requests.what: Neon light bar across the cab roof: a slim black housing, six lamps alternating CYAN and MAGENTA (glowing), end brackets and two small amber strobes at the ends.
Aggressive grille on the front fascia: dark slats, a CYAN glowing centre strip, angular ARMOR frame and small tow hooks below.
Remote weapon station on the roof ring: rotating armoured housing, twin short barrels with muzzle brakes, a camera eye glowing RED and an ammo box on the side.
Cargo in the bed: stacked ARMOR crates with CYAN stencil marks, a coil of cables, a glowing AMBER battery cell and tie-down straps.
Antenna array on the rear-left of the cab: one tall whip with a MAGENTA tip, a small dish and two shorter rods with blinking AMBER nodes.
Detail the outer face of the front-left hover pod: heat-vent louvres, a glowing CYAN status strip, bolted cover plates, and a fan hub inside the top intake.
Detail the outer face of the rear-right hover pod: heat-vent louvres, MAGENTA status strip, bolted plates, and a stabiliser fin angled outward.
Unit emblem on the left cab door: a hexagonal badge with a MAGENTA skull-and-circuit motif, small CYAN stencil numerals and a door handle plus armoured window slit trim.
Hood details: an angular armour scoop with CYAN glowing intake edge, two pairs of exposed bolts, a wiper rack at the windshield base and a thin MAGENTA hood-edge line.
Tailgate: licence holo-plate glowing CYAN, a wide RED light strip, hinge latches, and a pair of rear tow shackles.
Side skirts (skirtL and skirtR): hazard chevrons in AMBER and BLACK on the lower edge, scuffs and bolt rows.
Urban digital camo in HULL, HULL_DARK and METAL on hullSideL, hullSideR, hood and cab; faded grime near wheel pods and a neon CYAN pin stripe.
Tinted glass with faint CYAN scanlines and a HUD overlay (targeting reticle, small readouts), kept dark so glass reads.
Diamond-plate tread pattern in METAL and ARMOR with oil stains and a few glowing CYAN grid lines.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning a low-poly cyberpunk hover-pickup module, roughly 5.4m long, 2.0m wide, 1.9m tall, built from named parts with proper meta, REQUESTS, STAGE2 exports, and deciding it needs no joints since it's a static hovering vehicle sitting at ground level.

I'm laying out the truck geometry: body raised slightly off the floor with landing legs touching down, front hood from z 1.2 to 2.7, cab in the middle, and bed toward the rear, using extruded profiles for the cab silhouette and separate dark boxes for the windows.

For the windshield specifically, I'm placing a slanted rotated box to match the angle between the cab roof and hood points, working out the rotation around the x-axis so the glass sits flush against the sloped pillar line.

Now I'm adding the hover thrusters: four cylindrical nacelles positioned at the wheel locations with glowing cyan discs underneath, plus small landing skid feet touching the ground beneath each pod.

For the chassis, I'm blocking out the main body box, hood section, and bed floor with walls and neon trim rails, then adding a roll bar with a space reserved for a turret mount, along with militarized armor details like a front bumper, bull bar, angled side skirts, hood scoop, and exhaust stacks.

I'm also planning glow-based headlights and taillights, magenta underglow strips, and a set of extras like a roof light bar, grille, antenna array, bed cargo crates, side vents, and a holo plate, while naming the body side panels "hullSide" for texture mapping even though names might duplicate.

Deciding to split the side panels into hullSideL and hullSideR instead to avoid naming conflicts, I'm sketching a small box-building helper function and laying out body dimensions along the y-axis for the underbody and main side panels.

Working out the roof profile and windshield slope geometry, calculating the rotation angle and normal vector for the slanted glass, then setting the windshield width before moving on to define the bed walls and floor height.

Now I'm positioning the bed rails, tailgate, and front wall dimensions, then placing the exhaust stacks as small cylinders in the bed's front corners, and figuring out the side pod placement with their radius and connecting arm.

Still adding pod details...

I need to work out the skirt armor paint logic, adding hazard chevron stripes along the lower edge of the skirt box and bolt rows, using position-based coordinates to determine where the diagonal chevrons fall.

For the color type, I'll need to widen the box helper's color parameter to accept a Paint type alongside plain strings, importing the appropriate type from the builder module. I'll define the new paint constants before they're used, placing them near the chassis section, then swap the skirt and hull side references to use these new paints instead of the plain ARMOR color.

I'm switching the hood and cab to the CAMO paint, generating digital camo by quantizing position into grid cells and using noise to pick colors per cell, plus adding a cyan pin stripe along the upper edge and darkening the lower body for grime. For the windshield, I'm applying a dark glass texture with scanlines and a reticle onto the box geometry, accounting for how the rotation affects which face reads as the outward-facing surface.

Now I'm adding texture support to the box helper function and wiring the windshield part to use the new texture with white base color. For the bed floor, I'm painting a diamond plate pattern with noise-based oil stains and cyan grid lines, applied only to upward-facing surfaces.

I'm working out the pod FL geometry, with the cylinder dimensions, top intake, and rim sizing, then planning to add thin louvre boxes along the outer +X face.

Working out vertical placement now: the pod spans y 0.325 to 0.875, with radius interpolating from .36 to .44, and I'm fitting five louvres between y 0.45 and 0.7, plus a glowing cyan status strip near y 0.8. For the bolted plates, I'm computing surface positions along the faceted cylinder so they sit flush at z offsets around ±0.2-0.28, using the apothem geometry to find the right x depth.

Still working out plate positioning...

Settling on a dark teal color for the housing, then writing it out.
